caption: WER during fine-tuning Whisper model with different types of fine-tunning
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the Word Error Rate (WER) during the fine-tuning of Whisper models, specifically comparing two configurations: “tiny full” and “base full,” across six epochs. The x-axis represents the epoch number, ranging from 0 to 6 on a linear scale, with tick marks labeled at integer intervals. The y-axis represents the WER, scaled linearly from 20 to 29, with tick marks labeled at integer intervals. The “tiny full” model is depicted by a gray dashed line with triangle markers, starting at a WER of approximately 28.7 at epoch 0 and decreasing to about 22.8 at epoch 6. The “base full” model is shown by a blue dotted line with triangle markers, beginning at a WER of approximately 22.0 at epoch 0 and declining to about 19.0 at epoch 6. Both lines show a general downward trend in WER as training progresses, with the “tiny full” model starting with a higher WER than the “base full” model.
